Commentary.Commentary: Right then! That is it from this Test match as well as the series. Both teams share the trophy and now pose for the cameras. The cricketing action does not stop here as we have a lot of exciting action coming up as India take on Sri Lanka, while Australia will take on Pakistan in their respective Test series. The Women's World Cup, 2022 is also around the corner, so get ready for an exciting month ahead. We look forward to your company for all the games. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Dean Elgar, the skipper of South Africa, says that they wanted to take a bold decision of batting first and they are very happy with the result. Tells that after having lost the previous game, they wanted to make a strong comeback and he is very happy with the kind of character that his team showed in this Test. Says that they didn't do their basics right in the first Test and were eager to correct their mistakes this time around. Tells that they have some talented young players in their ranks and they will be looking to build a strong team going forward.

Tom Latham, the skipper of New Zealand, says that this is not the outcome they were looking for. Says that they were not able to build enough partnerships and weren't able to put a good first innings score. Tells that the game was in the balance for the majority of the match but the key moments didn't go their way. Adds that they knew South Africa were going to be at their best. Says that regardless of the conditions, they try to do better. Ends by thanking the South African team for coming to New Zealand.

Kagiso Rabada is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH. He says that it is never easy playing against New Zealand and says that when one plays, one needs to get the job done. Tells that they have been in such situations before. Adds that New Zealand were too good in the first Test but they had to win this one to make it 1-1. Informs that as a pacer, he would love to bowl on the wicket that was used in the first Test. Says that the lower order needed to step up with the bat and that's what they did. On Jamieson's catch, he says that it was a last-second decision to go for it and he is glad that he pulled it off.

Matt Henry is the PLAYER OF THE SERIES. He says that South Africa outplayed them in this match and they deserve to win. Adds that they fought hard but the South Africans were too good for them. Tells that he takes his batting very seriously and he enjoys batting out in the middle. Mentions that they wanted to take it ball-by-ball during the chase but failed to do so.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Keshav Maharaj is up for a quick chat. He says that it was nice to take the last wicket and end the proceedings. Mentions that the coaching staff put faith in him and thanks them for supporting him and giving him the opportunity. Adds that luckily the rain gods were on their side and managed to get them back on the field. Says that he just keeps bowling and bowling when he is not playing and tries to follow a routine. Informs that the coaches have been working with him in the nets and on the various aspects of his game

South Africa's second innings saw their wicketkeeper, Kyle Verreynne scoring his maiden Test hundred and Verreynne along with Rabada and Mulder made sure that New Zealand chase a mammoth total in the final innings. Well, chasing 426 runs was always going to be a tough ask and the Kiwis didn't get off to a good start either. Devon Conway and Tom Blundell dug in deep but they too perished at a crucial juncture in the game and then it was just a matter of time before they were bowled out. The lower order batters did show some fight but surviving the day was always going to be a huge challenge. Kagiso Rabada, Marco Jansen and Keshav Maharaj took three wickets apiece in the final innings and that ended New Zealand's hopes of winning a Test series against South Africa.

Earlier in the Test, it were the South African batters that set the tone for them as their opener Sarel Erwee notched up his maiden Test hundred. He was well-supported by the other batters which ensured that South Africa put on a good first innings total. Then with the ball, it was Kagiso Rabada who grabbed a five-wicket haul and apart from Daryl Mitchell and Colin de Grandhomme who brought up his second Test hundred, no other New Zealand batter looked promising, and as a result, South Africa got a healthy lead of 71 runs in the first innings.

What a comeback this has been from the Proteas after suffering a thumping defeat in the first Test. South Africa have managed to draw the series 1-1 and they are yet to lose a Test series against the Kiwis. It has been a complete team performance from them and they deserve to win this Test. New Zealand would be disappointed with the way they went about things in this Test, especially after a comprehensive win in the previous match but they have been completely outplayed by the tourists in the second Test.

OUT! LBW! Keshav Maharaj ends the proceedings. Took a little longer than what they would have wanted but doesn't matter as they have won this Test. Celebrations all around as South Africa win by 198 runs!

UPDATE - 8.05 am IST (2.35 am GMT) - Good news for South Africa and their fans as the covers have started to come off and it looks like it was just a passing shower. The play should resume after the Tea break unless the raingods have some other plans.

South Africa are just one wicket away from a victory now and it is just a matter of time before they get that! New Zealand's batters have worked hard but the bowling from the Proteas has been equally good. New Zealand headed into the Lunch break at the loss of Conway's wicket but it looked like it would take long for the South African bowlers to get the remaining wickets. However, they got success immediately after the break before it evaded them as Colin de Grandhomme was dropped. But Marco Jansen came in from the other end and kept bowling short. His ploy worked as Blundell and Colin de Grandhomme fell prey to it and then Kyle Jamieson and Tim Southee too followed them. South Africa are on the cusp of winning this Test and levelling the series but will have to wait a little longer. They will hope that the rain vanishes quickly and they wrap things up in the final session.

The Kiwis need 246 runs to win while South Africa require five wickets to level the series. We are in for another intriguing session which could also turn out to be the final one of this Test. Do join us for the post-Lunch session which begins at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT).

New Zealand started off well in the first session and it was Tom Blundell who came out with a positive intent of scoring runs. Conway also started to play some shots once he got his eye in and the Kiwis were scoring at a brisk rate. Although, Devon Conway fell short of his hundred and it was Lutho Sipamla who provided South Africa with the much-needed breakthrough. The South African bowlers have had to work hard for their wickets and it is Keshav Maharaj who has been the most impressing of them on this track. Also, the second new ball is due in 10 overs but South Africa would be keen to make the most damage before that.

The first session of Day 5 was always going to be crucial and at one point, it seemed like New Zealand would go unscathed into Lunch but the wicket of Conway has certainly turned the tide back in South Africa's favour. They did score 86 runs in the first session but have lost the key wicket of Conway.

South Africa set a mammoth target of 426 on Day 4 and then it was Rabada who breathed fire once again with the ball. New Zealand are 94/4 at the moment and Devon Conway looks settled but needs a massive support from others if they are to take the game deep. It will need a miracle from hereon to prevent the Proteas from levelling the series. They will look to give their all but as things stand, South Africa are in a pole position to win this Test and square the series. Can they script a famous win? Or will the Kiwis have something in store for us? All the answers coming your way shortly.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 5 - the final day of the second Test between New Zealand and South Africa. Day 4 turned out to be an enthralling one as the Proteas bossed the game and this Test is moving to an interesting finish. South Africa are on the cusp of a famous away victory after a poor first Test. The first hour is going to be a very crucial one for both the teams. Let's see how the day pans out.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

Right then, that is all we have from Day 4 of this Test match. It has been a day where South Africa have tightened their grip on this game and are just 6 wickets away from a memorable win at Hagley Oval. Can they script a famous win after being demolished in the first Test match on this very ground? Or will New Zealand display some character and resolve to save this Test. All the answers coming your way on Day 5. The first ball will be bowled at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, previous day). But as usual, our buildup will begin well in advance. Until then, goodbye and cheers!

New Zealand were quite poor on Day 4, to be honest. The bowling lacked penetration and the absence of a spinner in their attack will be a matter of discussion for sometime now. They could not put a lid on the scoring rate either and that meant that they were almost knocked out of the game with 426 runs to chase in the final innings. However, the worst was yet to come as they gave away three early wickets with the bat too. Conway and Mitchell had a decent partnership after that but Mitchell departed towards the fag end to make things even worse for the Blackcaps. The pitch is not that bad to bat on and if the Kiwis manage to apply themselves in the middle on Day 5, they might salvage a draw here, but a tough Day 5 awaits them.

South Africa have taken four wickets in this final session on a pitch that doesn’t have much for the bowlers in it. Rabada and Maharaj were always going to be key for them and they have delivered for their team again in this final session. Rabada sent back both the openers to the hut early and then Maharaj with his crafty spin-bowling got rid of Nicholls and well-set Mitchell to put South Africa right on top. Earlier in the day, they were fantastic with the bat too, as Kyle Verreynne notched up his maiden Test century and Rabada played a whirlwind cameo to post a huge target in front of the Blackcaps.

South Africa have finally managed to break the door and are now in a position where they are the only team that can win this game, at least realistically. After fighting hard for three days, New Zealand have been thoroughly outplayed on Day 4. They have six wickets in hand now and need to bat 90 overs on Day 5 to salvage a draw in this Test. A win for them is hard to imagine even if you put yourself into the shoes of a very optimistic Kiwi supporter.

On a length, on middle. Daryl Mitchell blocks it out.
This time he gets fuller on off. Daryl Mitchell defends it towards the off side off the front foot now.
Back of a length, around off at 133.8 kph. Daryl Mitchell blocks this off the back foot.
On a length, on off. Conway again defends this off the inside half of his blade to square leg. A single this time.
Goes fuller this time on off. Conway looks to drive it towards the off side but gets the inside half of his blade towards square leg.
Back of a length, on off. Conway defends it towards the leg side.
Another loopy delivery on off. Daryl Mitchell gets forward and blocks it out.
Nicely tossed up on middle. Daryl Mitchell pushes it towards mid on.
Slightly short on off. Conway goes back and pushes it towards mid on for a single.
A fuller delivery on middle. Daryl Mitchell drives it to mid on for a single.
Daryl Mitchell walks out to bat.

OUT! BOWLED! The spinner strikes on his second ball and New Zealand are in all sorts of trouble here! A slightly shorter delivery, around off. Henry Nicholls goes back to push it but completely misreads the turn here as the ball turns in sharply. The ball beats the inside edge of his blade and knocks over the middle pole. A big wicket this and Keshav Maharaj is showing his quality yet again.
Shorter and turning away around off. Henry Nicholls pushes it towards the off side.
Keshav Maharaj is into the attack now.
A fullish delivery on off. Conway drives it towards covers. Maharaj at short cover does well to stop it with a dive.
A good-length delivery, outside off and seaming away. Conway leaves it alone.
FOUR! A boundary this time! A full toss on the pads. Conway just flicks this off his pads towards the square leg fence for a boundary.
Back of a length, on middle. Henry Nicholls gets on the top of the bounce and nudges it towards the leg side for a single.
Shorter length and around leg. Henry Nicholls lets it go.
A good-length delivery, on off and nipping into the batter. Conway defends this off the inside half of his blade towards mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length, on middle. Henry Nicholls nudges it towards the leg side.
Short delivery on middle. Conway pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
On a length, on middle. Henry Nicholls works it towards mid-wicket and takes a quick single.
A full ball, on middle. Devon Conway flicks it through the mid-wicket region. The batters take three runs.
Back of a length, angled down leg. Conway gets inside the line of the ball and leaves it alone.
This is a length ball, around off that jags back in late. Devon Conway looks to defend but it goes off the inner half of the blade towards square leg.
Back of a length, around off. Henry Nicholls stands tall and blocks it out.
A bit fuller this time, on middle. Henry Nicholls prods and drives it to mid on.
A length ball, jagging back in from middle. Henry Nicholls tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Good-length ball, around off. Conway hangs back to defend but it goes off the outside edge towards the slip fielder, along the ground.
Back of a length, around off. Henry Nicholls gets on top of the bounce and defends it.
A short ball, on off. Henry Nicholls ducks underneath.
Jansen darts it on the pads. Henry Nicholls flicks it to deep square leg for one run.
Good-length ball, angling away from outside off. Henry Nicholls leaves it alone.
On a length, around off. Henry Nicholls blocks it off the front foot.
Another ball that is short of a length, outside off. Henry Nicholls looks to cut hard but does not time it well.
Short and wide, outside off. Henry Nicholls looks to cut but it takes the underedge and lands into the deck.
A bumper, around off. Devon Conway mistimes his pull towards the fine leg fielder on the bounce. A single taken.
Rabada hits the deck hard, on middle. Henry Nicholls stays back and gets solid in his defence.
Short of a length, on off. Henry Nicholls keeps it out.
A low full toss, on middle. Henry Nicholls drags it to mid on.
Good-length delivery, on middle. Henry Nicholls presses forward to block it.
A length ball, around off. Henry Nicholls defends it out.
An appeal for LBW but turned down! A yorker-length ball, angling in from middle. Henry Nicholls fails to dig it out and gets hit on his pad. Might have gone down leg.
On a length, just outside off. Devon Conway lets it sail through to the keeper.
A bit full and on middle. Nicholls nudges it wide of mid-wicket and takes a single.
On a length, on middle. Henry Nicholls works it towards mid-wicket and takes a quick single.
Shorter in length, outside off. Devon Conway shuffles across a bit and helps it on its way towards deep square leg for a single.
Short of a length, outside off. Devon Conway leaves it alone.
Jansen serves a length ball, jagging back in from off. Devon Conway keeps it out.
Good-length ball, around middle. Henry Nicholls looks to defend but it goes off the thick inside edge towards the short leg fielder.
Drop and run! On a length, outside off. Conway taps it to the off side and sets off for a quick run.
Rabada hits the deck hard, around off. Devon Conway covers the line of the ball and defends it out.
Back of a length, around off. Devon Conway prods and blocks it.

DROPPED! Back of a length, angling in from off and cramping the batter for room. Devon Conway looks to pull but he miscues it and the ball goes left of the backward square leg fielder. The fielder dives to his left and gets both hands on it but fails to pouch it.
Back of a length, on middle. Henry Nicholls nudges it wide of mid-wicket for a run.
Good-length delivery, otutside off. Devon Conway does not offer any shot to this one.
On a length, around off. Devon Conway keeps it out.
Jansen bangs it into the deck, on middle. Henry Nicholls pulls it along the ground behind square on the leg side for a single.
Another ball, on a length, just outside off and jagging back in late. Henry Nicholls lets it be and the ball goes just past the off pole.
Good-length delivery, just outside off. Henry Nicholls leaves it alone.
Short of a length, down leg. Henry Nicholls sways away from the line of the ball.
Back of a length, around middle. Devon Conway keeps it out.
A good-length delivery around off. Conway goes pushing for it but the ball beats the outside edge of his blade.
Another good-length delivery angling across the left-hander and Conway lets it go.
A length delivery, outside off. Conway lets it go.
A length ball, around middle. Henry Nicholls tucks it to the leg side for a run.

OUT! TAKEN! Rabada strikes again and sends back the Kiwi skipper! Rabada goes back of a length, on middle, angling into the body. Latham just tries to work it away towards the leg side but ends up hitting it towards the short leg fielder and Rassie van der Dussen there takes a sharp catch. Big wicket this and Kiwis are in early trouble here. Henry Nicholls is the next man in.
Commentary.Howout: c Rassie van der Dussen b Kagiso Rabada

Commentary.Commentary: Another length delivery, outside off. Conway leaves it again.
A good-length delivery, outside off. Conway leaves it alone.
On a length and angling across the batter. Devon Conway lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length, around off. Conway blocks it.
BEATEN! On a length, just outside off. Conway has a poke at it but the ball beats his outside edge.
A length ball, angling down leg. Devon Conway misses his flick.
Marco Jansen will share the new ball with Kagiso Rabada.
A length ball, angling in from middle. Devon Conway clips it behind square on the leg side and takes a run.
FOUR! EDGY! Good-length ball, around off. Devon Conway looks to block but it goes off the outside edge past the slip fielder and into the fence.
A short ball, angling down leg. Devon Conway leaves it alone.
Devon Conway walks in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! South Africa are off to a dream start! Rabada strikes in his first over and New Zealand lose a wicket early on. Rabada serves a full ball, outside off. Will Young looks for a booming drive but it takes the outside edge and goes straight to Temba Bavuma at gully who makes no mistake. Young departs for a duck and South Africa are on top! Not the kind of start that New Zealand would be hoping for!
Commentary.Howout: c Temba Bavuma b Kagiso Rabada

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, outside off. Will Young leaves it alone.
Good-length ball, around off. Tom Latham taps it to the off side and takes a single. New Zealand are underway!
